- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"

</example>

<example>

user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>

Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>

The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

82	    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). 110	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
111	
112	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.
113	
114	## Overrides Pattern
115	
116	All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
117	
118	**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
119	
120	**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
121	
122	1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
123	2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
124	3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
125	4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**
126

160	## Contentful Content Type Management
161	
162	Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.
163	
164	**Key paths:**
165	
166	- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
167	- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)
168	
169	**To register a new content type:**
170	
171	1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
172	2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
173	
174	**To run the sync:**
175	
176	```
177	npm run sync:contentful
178	```
179	
180	Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account — in `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold it, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running the sync). Get the token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
181	
182	The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).
183	
184	**Relationship to the React component:**
185	Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.
186	
187	**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

204	## Integration Map
205	
206	All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.
207	
208	**Boundary key:**
209	
210	- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
211	- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
212	- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
213	- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
214	- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
215	- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
216	- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

244	| **Shippit / Ordoro**                 | Carrier label automation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | OMS-level only                                                                                                                                                                                | SFCC passes address to MuleSoft, not directly to these                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
245	| **Google Business API**              | Store hours feed (boutique opening hours)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Out-of-band (daily feed into SFCC)                                                                                                                                                            | Consumed by Find in Boutique / store-locator UI — PWA renders, does not call Google directly                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
246	| **Feedonomics**                      | Product feed for downstream marketing channels (PRD-071)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Out-of-band                                                                                                                                                                                   | No PWA runtime touchpoint; flagged for SEO/marketing dependency awareness only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
247	| **Measmerize**                       | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP (PRD-050–053)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | PWA-direct (script injection on PDP only)                                                                                                                                                     | Browser-direct; no MRT proxy. Script injected once on PDP mount; widget self-determines product availability and signals the PWA via events. Falls back to the Contentful size guide when Measmerize has no data for the product. **Consent approach unconfirmed — open item.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
248	
249	## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
250	
251	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.
252	
253	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
254	
255	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.
256	
257	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
258	
259	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
260	
261	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
262	
263	```ts
264	import { Pool } from 'undici';
265	
266	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
267	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
268	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
269	  timeout: 8000,
270	});
271	
272	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
273	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
274	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
275	    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
276	  });
277	}
278	```
279	
280	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
281	
282	| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                            | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
283	| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
284	| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                            | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
285	| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
286	| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                               | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
287	| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange                               | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections.                                                                                                           |
288	| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password)                      | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load.                                                                                                                                                |
289	| `google-places`        | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New)                                                                | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059)                    | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly.                                                                                                                      |
290	| `booxi`                | Booxi base URL (TBD — confirm with Integration team)                                                              | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167)                           | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

# Architecture

_Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made._

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, eight storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with both EU and US each split into two storefronts (domestic + international).

## Pre-Build Decisions

These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.

| #   | Decision                     | Status                                 |
| --- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Browser & device matrix      | ✅ Confirmed (informal)                |
| 2   | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending       |
| 3   | Performance budgets          | ✅ Confirmed (informal)                |
| 4   | Client-side error reporting  | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool             |
| 5   | Feature-flag tool            | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
| 6   | Translation fallback chain   | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending       |

### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅

**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.

### #2 — Accessibility 🟡

**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.

### #3 — Performance budgets ✅

**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.

### #6 — Translation fallback 🟡

[regional.md](./prd/regional.md) REG-046: "English is the site-wide fallback." Doesn't disambiguate `en-eu` vs `en`, nor split by content type.
**Pending Brand/Legal decision** on the rule per content type:

| Content type | Suggested chain          | Why                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| UI strings   | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → `en` | Universal meaning                            |
| Editorial    | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Avoid half-translated pages                  |
| Product copy | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Care/sizing are region-specific (regulatory) |

REG-047 (Contentful↔Transperfect↔SFCC workflow) remains separately TBC.

### Accepted risks

**#4 — No client-side error reporting.** JS errors in customer browsers (e.g. Adyen iframe failure on a specific iOS Safari version) are invisible to the team; detection relies on support tickets. Revisit post-launch if checkout completion dips unexplained.

**#5 — No feature-flag tool.** Optimizely Web Experimentation ([analytics.md](./prd/analytics.md) AAB-004) covers analytics A/B. Note (confirmed 09-06): Optimizely is **not** a GTM tag — the PWA loads its script directly in the page head (US storefront only, single snippet across environments, before render to avoid flicker), Didomi-gated. Progressive rollout, social login dark-launch, and August-2026 payment-method gating will be handled via deploy timing and branch merges — no instant kill-switch, no % rollouts.

## Frontend Stack

### Bundled by PWA Kit

| Layer                        | Library                                               | Notes                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base framework               | PWA Kit v3+                                           | Salesforce storefront foundation                                                      |
| UI framework                 | React 18 + Chakra UI                                  | Component library + theme system                                                      |
| Routing                      | React Router v6                                       |                                                                                       |
| Server/async state           | TanStack Query (via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) | All SFCC data fetching                                                                |
| i18n                         | react-intl                                            | Translations in `translations/`                                                       |
| Build + dev server           | Webpack 5 (via `pwa-kit-dev`)                         |                                                                                       |
| Build + test runner (legacy) | Jest (via `pwa-kit-dev test`)                         | `jest.config.js` — kept for PWA Kit internals; superseded by Vitest for project tests |

### Project additions

| Layer                                  | Library                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Type safety                            | TypeScript strict mode                         | `tsconfig.json`                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Component explorer + interaction tests | Storybook 8                                    | `storybook dev -p 6006`; `play` functions are the primary tool for component-level interaction testing                                                                                                              |
| Storybook a11y addon                   | `@storybook/addon-a11y`                        | Component-level accessibility checks during development and in Storybook test runs                                                                                                                                  |
| Unit test runner                       | Vitest                                         | `vitest.config.ts`; replaces `pwa-kit-dev test` for project tests                                                                                                                                                   |
| Accessibility testing                  | axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) | Automated WCAG checks in unit and E2E layers; see Pre-Build Decisions #2 for outstanding items                                                                                                                      |
| E2E tests (planned)                    | Playwright                                     | Not yet configured                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Forms + validation                     | react-hook-form + zod                          | Not yet installed; add when checkout/account work begins                                                                                                                                                            |
| Global UI state                        | Zustand                                        | For shared state that outgrows Context (multi-step flows, drawer state, etc.). **SSR note:** initialise store per-request — never as a module singleton — to prevent state leaking across server-rendered requests. |

### External services

Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.

## Environments

Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |

**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.

**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.

**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.

## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)

Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

## Overrides Pattern

All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.

**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.

**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:

1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

## New vs. Override Components

- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.

## Key Paths

- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); per-component overrides live one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2). Register a new component override in `components/index.ts`.
- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`

## Design Source of Truth

Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.

Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.

## Header Layout (based on draft Figma, subject to change)

Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.

**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.

**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread _after_ `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.

**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.

**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.

## Contentful Content Type Management

Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.

**Key paths:**

- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)

**To register a new content type:**

1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`

**To run the sync:**

```
npm run sync:contentful
```

Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account — in `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold it, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running the sync). Get the token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.

The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).

**Relationship to the React component:**
Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.

**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

## Path Aliases

Configured in four places (keep in sync):

- `babel.config.js` — `babel-plugin-module-resolver` (covers `npm start` dev server + `npm run build`)
- `tsconfig.json` — `baseUrl` + `paths` (TypeScript / VS Code intellisense)
- `.storybook/main.js` — `webpackFinal` alias
- `jest.config.js` — `moduleNameMapper` (PWA Kit internals)
- `vitest.config.ts` — `resolve.alias` (project tests)

| Alias | Resolves to     |
| ----- | --------------- |
| `~`   | project root    |
| `app` | `overrides/app` |

## Integration Map

All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.

**Boundary key:**

- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

| System                               | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Boundary                                                                                                                                                                                      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC)** | Storefront, product catalogue, order management (record of truth), customer accounts, Business Manager config                                                                                                                                                                                   | —                                                                                                                                                                                             | Domestic checkout owner                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)

Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.

## Blast-Radius Mitigation

Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.

The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

```ts
import { Pool } from 'undici';

// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
  timeout: 8000,
});

// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
  });
}
```

134	## 4. Customisation Model
135	
136	This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's _template extensibility_ model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.
137	
138	All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.
139	
140	**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.
141	
142	**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.
143

168	**Security policy:**
169	
170	- Real values live only in local, untracked environment files — one shared file (`.env.shared`, tier-independent) plus one per deployment tier (`.env.<tier>` for dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). Only a template — variable names tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on their own comment line, no secret values — is committed to source control as `.env.sample`. Two guardrails enforce this: a pre-commit hook that blocks commit if `.env.sample` contains a secret-shaped non-empty value, and a Claude Code rule that instructs the AI assistant never to write real secret values into `.env.sample`.
171	- Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
172	- Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
173	- Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
174	- MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

197	### 5.2 Entry routing
198	
199	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
200	- **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
201	- **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.
202	
203	### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale
204	
205	Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.
206	
207	### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed
208	
209	- **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
210	- **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
211	- **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
212	- **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.
213	
214	### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts
215	
216	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):
217	
218	- **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
219	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
220	- **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
221	- **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

225	## 6. Checkout Ownership Branching
226	
227	Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.
228	
229	- **SFCC owns:** AU domestic (including Oceania — Avalara for NZ + New Caledonia), UK, US (when shipping to US), EU domestic.
230	- **Global-e owns:** HK, ME, EU international, the US site when shipping outside the US, and any domestic storefront when the selected shipping destination is outside that storefront's market.
231	- **Pricing for Global-e markets (REG-041):** SFCC holds all pricebooks (including Global-e ones), derived nightly from AP21 base prices and Global-e FX/coefficients. SFCC sends the complete cart in target currency at handoff; Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from that point. Full mechanism specified under PRC-34..43.
232	- **Global-e shipping country lock (REG-028):** locked at the country selector pre-checkout; cannot change once inside Global-e.

236	## 7. Integration Map
237	
238	### 7.1 Classification model
239	
240	Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.
241	
242	- **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
243	- **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
244	- **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
245	- **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
246	- **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).
247	
248	A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.
249	
250	> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.
