292	### 7.3 Contentful schema as code
293	
294	Content type definitions live in version control and are deployed to Contentful via an idempotent sync script (`npm run sync:contentful`) using a Contentful Management Token. The script is field-additive — it will not delete fields from a live content type. Each definition pairs with a typed React component, so schema changes are reviewable and repeatable. Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module.
295	
296	### 7.4 Non-system stakeholders
297	
298	Parties that influence the build but are not systems the storefront integrates with at runtime. Their deliverables hand over to Accenture for implementation.
299	
300	| Party                                          | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Handover to Accenture                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
301	| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
302	| **Sparro**                                     | External SEO consultancy. Defines the JSON-LD schema templates (PDP, PLP, boutique, homepage — DMU-037 to DMU-040), the consolidated hreflang structure (DMU-025), and the CMS-editable on-page SEO field schema (DMU-035).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Specification documents per requirement ID; Accenture implements in SFCC / PWA. Final JSON-LD scope and page types to be confirmed before build (DMU-038).                                                                                                                                                |
303	| **Accessibility vendor** _(TBC by Zimmermann)_ | Manual accessibility audits, screen-reader and assistive-tech testing, audit cadence, remediation triage. Complements the automated coverage in §10.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Audit reports per cadence; defects raised back into the Accenture backlog. Vendor name, screen-reader / browser matrix, and cadence still pending from Zimmermann.                                                                                                                                        |
304	| **Tell No Lies**                               | Zimmermann's marketing technology partner. Owns the GTM container configuration and the downstream tags loaded inside GTM (GA4, Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, etc.). The container is hosted on **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned managed tagging server) — Tell No Lies operates the Addingwell workspace, not just the GTM container. **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg** are loaded as PWA-direct head tags; Optimizely's script is supplied by Zimmermann. | Accenture's responsibility ends at emitting a comprehensive data layer (AAB-001 / AAB-002), embedding the GTM container ID + Addingwell tagging-server URL, and injecting the Optimizely/Crazy Egg head snippets (Didomi-gated). Tell No Lies consumes the data layer and configures the GTM-housed tags. |
305	
306	---
307	
308	## 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
309	
310	### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)
311	
312	All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.
313	
314	#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type
315	
316	PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.
317	
318	| Page type                                                         | Pattern                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                            |
319	| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
320	| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages                | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server                                                                                                                                                                | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical                                                                                                                                                                     |
321	| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
322	| Search results, filtered PLP states                               | **SSR shell + CSR data**                                                                                                                                                                                             | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven                                                                                                                                        |
323	
324	The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.
325	
326	### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang
327	
328	Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.
329	
330	### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots
331	
332	Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.
333	
334	### 8.4 Structured data
335	
336	Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:
337	
338	- **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
339	- **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
340	- **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
341	- **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).
342	
343	### 8.5 URL strategy
344	
345	- Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
346	- Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
347	- 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.
348	
349	### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)
350	
351	No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.
352	
353	---
354	
355	## 9. Performance Strategy
356	
357	LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.
358	
359	| Metric                    | Target |
360	| ------------------------- | ------ |
361	| LCP (mobile p75)          | ≤ 2 s  |
362	| Lighthouse Performance    | ≥ 0.80 |
363	| Lighthouse Accessibility  | ≥ 0.90 |
364	| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |
365	
366	### 9.1 Third-party defer rule
367	
368	Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.
369	
370	### 9.2 Other levers
371	
372	- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
373	- **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
374	  - **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
375	  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
376	  - Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
377	- Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
378	- Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.
379	
380	### 9.3 Where performance is measured
381	
382	The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.
383	
384	> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.
385	
386	---
387	
388	## 10. Accessibility
389	
390	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, with WCAG 2.1 AA as the floor that is always met.
391	
392	**Automated coverage:**
393	
394	- axe-core via `vitest-axe` at the unit layer and `axe-playwright` at the E2E layer
395	- Storybook a11y addon at component level during development
396	- Lighthouse CI accessibility score ≥ 0.90 in the SIT gate
397	
398	**Manual coverage:** delegated to Zimmermann's existing accessibility vendor (unconfirmed — vendor, screen-reader / browser matrix, and audit cadence to be supplied by Zimmermann).
399	
400	---
401	
402	## 11. Consent & Marketing
403	
404	### 11.1 Didomi gating (REG-048–056)
405	
406	- Cookie consent banner on first visit, all storefronts; preferences persist across sessions and are reviewable/updatable per category at any time.
407	- **No third-party tracking or marketing script loads until consent is granted** — including GTM (and the tags Tell No Lies loads downstream: Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, GA4, etc.), the PWA-direct head tags Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg (AAB-004/005), Inside Chat, Narvar widgets.
408	- **reCAPTCHA is not a tracking script** (CRM-008). It loads on register / login form interaction only, deferred to keep it off LCP. **Regional split:** in **EU & UK** it is consent-gated and loads only after Didomi consent — with the accepted consequence that a visitor who declines consent is never challenged, so reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection there. In **all other regions** it loads on form interaction regardless of consent state.
409	- GTM integrated with Didomi for **Google Consent Mode v2**; hashed email passed at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions.
410	- Where consent state cannot be determined, the system **fails closed** — no third-party scripts load.
411	- Per-storefront consent defaults are specified under REG-054.
412	
413	### 11.2 Marketing opt-in sync
414	
415	`FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys` is the opt-in sync chain (REG-058, REG-059). Sync failures queue and retry silently — they never block the user flow. Trigger points (guest at order placement, registered at registration and My Account preference updates) are functional detail, out of scope for this TSD.
416	
417	### 11.3 GDPR touchpoints in the PWA
418	
419	GDPR fulfilment (DSAR, right-to-erasure, retention, breach reporting per REG-060–067) is handled by the SFCC GDPR cartridge and BM configuration — out of scope for this TSD. PWA-side touchpoints are limited to:
420	
421	- Localised privacy policy pages, served from Contentful per storefront.
422	- The consent UI itself (covered in 11.1).
423	- Surfacing the customer-initiated erasure / data-export entry point in My Account where exposed by SFCC.
424	
425	### 11.4 Didomi consent gate reference
426	
427	Implementation reference for the PWA: which Didomi purpose / vendor ID gates each third-party script. All IDs are **TBC — none have been received from Zimmermann yet.** Guesses are in brackets to orient the conversation.
428	
429	> Didomi purpose IDs for the three declared categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051), plus per-environment Notice IDs, are open items (§12.1 / §12.2 of the Open Items register). All vendor-specific IDs below depend on those being provisioned first.
430	
431	| Integration                                                          | Didomi purpose / vendor ID                                          | Scope                                  | Open item ref |
432	| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
433	| **GTM (Addingwell)** — loads Meta, GA4, Pinterest, TikTok downstream | Handled by Tell No Lies in the GTM container / Addingwell workspace | All storefronts                        | —             |
434	| **Inside Chat**                                                      | TBC                                                                 | All storefronts                        | §14.1         |
435	| **Optimizely Web**                                                   | TBC (Analytics?)                                                    | US storefront only                     | §15.2         |
436	| **Crazy Egg**                                                        | TBC (Analytics?)                                                    | All storefronts                        | §16.3         |
437	| **Narvar Promise**                                                   | TBC (Analytics/Performance? from Narvar/Zimm?)                      | Domestic storefronts only              | §11.2         |
438	| **reCAPTCHA v3**                                                     | n/a — no consent required; loads on form interaction                | All except EU & UK                     | —             |
439	| **reCAPTCHA v3**                                                     | TBC                                                                 | EU & UK storefronts only               | §10.2         |
440	| **Measmerize**                                                       | TBC                                                                 | PDP only                               | §17.1         |
441	| **Vimeo**                                                            | TBC (Marketing/Analytics? use `dnt=1` if no consent)                | PDP + editorial pages, all storefronts | §18.1         |
442	
443	---
444	
445	## 12. Graceful Degradation
446	
447	Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.

# Technical Solution Design — PWA (Architecture)

_Last updated 2026-07-16. Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet._

---

## 1. Purpose & Scope

This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.

**In scope:**

- Stack and build pipeline
- The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
- Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 8 storefronts in 6 regions
- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
- SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
- Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
- Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
- Open decisions requiring client input before build

**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

---

## 2. Solution Overview

A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

## 4. Customisation Model

This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's _template extensibility_ model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.

All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.

**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.

**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.

**Security policy:**

- Real values live only in local, untracked environment files — one shared file (`.env.shared`, tier-independent) plus one per deployment tier (`.env.<tier>` for dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). Only a template — variable names tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on their own comment line, no secret values — is committed to source control as `.env.sample`. Two guardrails enforce this: a pre-commit hook that blocks commit if `.env.sample` contains a secret-shaped non-empty value, and a Claude Code rule that instructs the AI assistant never to write real secret values into `.env.sample`.
- Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
- Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
- Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
- MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

## 5. Multi-Site, Multi-Locale Architecture

### 5.1 Storefronts

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions**, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods. 11 active locales total. US/EU domestic and international are configured as separate SFCC sites (REG-006).

| Locale                          | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner          |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| AU + Oceania                    | `/` (x-default hreflang)                   | AUD                    | SFCC (REG-003)          |
| UK                              | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC (REG-004)          |
| US domestic                     | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (REG-005)          |
| US international                | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (REG-005)      |
| EU domestic — EN / FR / IT / ES | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC (REG-006 dom)      |
| EU international                | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK                              | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-007)      |
| ME                              | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-008)      |

Rest-of-world traffic routes via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` (DMU-013). AU is configured at the root with no locale prefix and serves as the x-default hreflang target (DMU-016).

### 5.2 Entry routing

- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
- **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.

### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale

Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.

### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed

- **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
- **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
- **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
- **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.

### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

- **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
- **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
- **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

## 6. Checkout Ownership Branching

Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.

- **SFCC owns:** AU domestic (including Oceania — Avalara for NZ + New Caledonia), UK, US (when shipping to US), EU domestic.
- **Global-e owns:** HK, ME, EU international, the US site when shipping outside the US, and any domestic storefront when the selected shipping destination is outside that storefront's market.
- **Pricing for Global-e markets (REG-041):** SFCC holds all pricebooks (including Global-e ones), derived nightly from AP21 base prices and Global-e FX/coefficients. SFCC sends the complete cart in target currency at handoff; Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from that point. Full mechanism specified under PRC-34..43.
- **Global-e shipping country lock (REG-028):** locked at the country selector pre-checkout; cannot change once inside Global-e.

## 7. Integration Map

### 7.1 Classification model

Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.

- **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
- **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
- **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
- **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
- **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).

A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.

> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

## 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)

All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type

PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.

| Page type                                                         | Pattern                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages                | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server                                                                                                                                                                | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states                               | **SSR shell + CSR data**                                                                                                                                                                                             | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven                                                                                                                                        |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang

Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots

Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data

Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:

- **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
- **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
- **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
- **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy

- Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
- Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
- 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)

No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

## 9. Performance Strategy

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric                    | Target |
| ------------------------- | ------ |
| LCP (mobile p75)          | ≤ 2 s  |
| Lighthouse Performance    | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility  | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers

- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
  - **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  - Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
- Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
- Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

460	### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment
461	
462	The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the _spread_ of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.
463	
464	#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)
465	
466	- **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
467	- **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.
468	
469	#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)
470	
471	`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
472	
473	> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.
474	
475	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
476	
477	| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                             | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
478	| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
479	| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                             | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
480	| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
481	| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                                | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |

### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment

The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the _spread_ of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.

#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)

- **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
- **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.

#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)

`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                             | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                             | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                                | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                  | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange                               | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections.                                                                                                           |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                  | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password)                      | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load.                                                                                                                                                |
| `google-places`        | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New)                                                                 | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059)                    | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly.                                                                                                                      |
| `booxi`                | Booxi base URL (TBD)                                                                                               | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167)                           | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).
